Our primary endpoint was to evaluate the dermal toxicity of
endoxifen gel at the application site (skin of both breasts) compared to
placebo gel, in an intent to treat analysis that included all participants
who initiated study treatment. Dose limiting toxicity (DLT) was defined
as Grade ≥ 2, using modified CTCAE criteria for the parameters shown
in Table S1, occurring at the application site for 48 h or longer and
definitely, probably, or possibly related to the study drug, or be a cause
for participant withdrawal. Adverse event frequencies were summarized
using the highest-grade for each adverse event type for all participants
who initiated treatment and separately for each dose level.
Secondary endpoints included the assessments of 1) participant-
reported symptoms related to use of endoxifen gel in comparison to
placebo gel using CTCAE criteria and BESS questionnaire [26], 2) breast
and plasma concentrations of endoxifen (E) and (Z) isomers at each dose
level (10 mg and 20 mg daily), and 3) tamoxifen responsive circulating
markers (IGF1 and SHBG) [11]. The results were reported using median
and interquartile range (IQR). Non-adherent participants were excluded
from analysis of secondary endpoints, with the exception of the patient
reported symptom survey (BESS). Median per-patient concentration was
defined as median concentration across all sampled locations in one or
both breasts. Entire breast concentration was defined as the median
concentration across the five sampling locations in each breast (Fig. 2A).
If tumor drug concentration was available, a summary value per breast
including the tumor was also generated. For each treatment arm,
within-participant changes were assessed using the Wilcoxon signed
rank test. Differences between treatment arms were assessed using the
Wilcoxon rank sum test and the Kruskal-Wallis test. Linear mixed models
with random intercepts to account for correlation of endoxifen con-
centrations across multiple locations within participant and breast were
fitted to assess the potential effect of tissue adiposity, epithelial cellu-
larity, BMI, use of tumescence solution during surgery, and breast size
on log10-transformed breast tissue concentration. Breast size (large vs.
small & medium) was estimated by combining bra band, cup size, (or
mastectomy weight, if bra band or cup size information were missing).
